newsitem.title: USA: Dropout, others sought for leads in Levin slaying.
newsitem.headline: Dropout, others sought for leads in Levin slaying.

text.p: Police were seeking a high-school dropout and others Friday for questioning in the murder of the son of Time Warner Inc's top executive, police sources said.
The sources said the 19-year-old dropout identified as Corey Arthur was a former student of the slain man, Jonathan Levin, at New York's Taft High School.

Levin, 31, the son of Time Warner chief executive and chairman Gerald Levin, was found Monday shot once in the head at his one-bedroom Manhattan apartment. He had been bound and gagged and there was no sign of forced entry.
Police believe Levin was murdered for his automatic teller machine card and was jabbed with a steak knife until he revealed the personal code that gave access to the cash dispenser.
A police spokesman said there had been no arrests. "We don't have a suspect at this time," he told Reuters.
However, the sources said investigators learned Arthur's first name from Levin's telephone answering machine last Friday, the day authorities believe he was killed.
Arthur left a message on Levin's machine, saying, "I need to see you. It's important." Police also are looking for several other people for questioning.
Investigators believe the killer shot Levin, then raced to a Chase Manhattan Bank branch a few blocks away and withdrew $800.
Authorities have a picture from a bank security camera of a man withdrawing money from Levin's account. However, the photo is too fuzzy for positive identification.
Levin was a beloved English teacher at Taft, a public school in New York's poor South Bronx section. He often befriended students and had only recently told some of them of his wealthy background.
WCBS-AM radio reported police wanted to speak to Arthur after overnight questioning of an informant.
His mother, Penny Bostick, told The New York Post newspaper her son had not lived with her for a year.
"I don't see him much. If I knew where he was, I would call the police," she said.
